Performers
María Barrientos (soprano), Manuel de Falla (piano) Documented

DAHR lists both as personnel for matrix WLX310; the Archivo Manuel de Falla credits them together for the cycle in its 2021 exhibition.

[1] [2] [4]
Work version
Voice and piano, the fourth song of the cycle Documented

DAHR describes the recording as soprano vocal solo with piano. The published edition used and the key sung are not stated in the sources consulted.

[1] [2]
Recorded
1928-03-31 Documented

DAHR gives 31 March 1928 for matrix WLX310 from Michael Gray’s compilation of the Columbia recording logs. The Archivo Manuel de Falla’s 2021 exhibition credits give 1930 for other songs of the cycle (Nana, Asturiana), and a 2022 review dates the whole recording between 1928 and 1930.

[1]
Place
Paris, France Documented

DAHR cites Copeland for the recording location; the studio is not named.

[1]
Label
Columbia (France/Belgium) Documented

Twelve-inch 78-rpm disc; the Internet Archive item gives the publisher as French Columbia.

[1] [2]
Catalogue
PFX-1 Documented

DAHR lists the Jota under Columbia (France/Belgium) PFX-1; the second file of the Internet Archive item is named for Columbia PFX-1.

[1] [3]
Matrix, take, sides
Matrix WLX310, take 1 (master) Documented

The transfer is a single side lasting 3:05; which face of PFX-1 carries the Jota is not stated.

[1]
Transfer
Internet Archive 78rpm collection Documented

Item in the Internet Archive’s 78-rpm opera collection; no personal mastering credit is given.

[2]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The item was uploaded on 22 November 2019; the date of the transfer itself is not stated.

[2]
Processing
Digitised at 78 rpm; stylus size “40e” as stated in the item Documented

Equalisation, noise reduction and any restoration settings are not stated.

[2]
Composition rights
Falla died on 14 November 1946. Spanish law protects the works of authors who died before 7 December 1987 for life plus 80 years, so his music remains protected in Spain until the end of 2026; arrangements and modern editions carry their own rights Documented

A phonogram term assessment does not clear the composition, an arrangement or a modern score edition.

[8] [9]
Recording rights
Territorial EU phonogram public-domain basis: issued on Columbia PFX-1 in or after mid-1930, a 78-rpm disc, before 1963 Inferred, not documented

DAHR places the session in March 1928 and the disc in Columbia’s French catalogue (PFX-1). The Marston track list for its Supervia volume 5 pairs the Jota (matrix WLX 310, 31 March 1928) on PFX-1 with Nana and Canción (WLX 1368, recorded 3 June 1930), so the disc cannot have appeared before mid-1930; the Archivo Manuel de Falla’s credits give 1930 for other songs of the cycle. No dated advertisement, review or catalogue giving the issue date of PFX-1 was found. The Marston restoration of the Jota runs 3:08 against 3:05 here, so this transfer may run slightly fast. This is a territorial phonogram basis, not US or worldwide clearance and not a Creative Commons licence.

Falla, Siete canciones populares españolas, No. 4, Jota; María Barrientos, soprano; Manuel de Falla, piano. Columbia (France/Belgium) PFX-1, Internet Archive transfer. Territorial EU phonogram basis only; Falla’s composition remains protected in Spain until the end of 2026.
